quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in a school zone if no other sign is posted?
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a school zone is 15 mph. Drive slowly and carefully in school zones because children and other pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle starts to skid?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to help the vehicle regain balance. Steer in the direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding to regain control.

questions.question: If you park in an unusual location, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions
Park five feet away from the curb

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions
questions.explanation: You are responsible for parking safely so your vehicle is not a hazard. Make sure your car is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line in the center of a road mean?

options.text: No one is allowed to pass from either direction
Drivers may pass from either direction when it is safe

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass from either direction when it is safe
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this orange triangle symbol mean?
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, roadwork machinery, or horse-drawn wagons. During the day it is orange. At night it appears as a red hollow triangle.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line mean on a highway?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes if it is safe
You may only cross to change lanes if you are in the left lane

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes if it is safe
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have exited
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully
Stop until the red lights stop flashing

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights turn off. You do not need to stop if the bus is on the other side of a divided highway.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road?

options.text: Keep driving at the speed limit to get through it
Shift to neutral while driving through the water

questions.explanation: To prevent skidding, avoid slippery areas such as ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles. The safest surface for driving is dry and solid.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you
Honk your horn to alert them

questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind or partially blind pedestrian. You must yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning happen?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is water on the road. At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires push water away. At speeds above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. Your tires may lose grip and slide over the water like water skis.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. They may suddenly change direction. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see, so be extra careful.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show blind spots. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in these hidden areas.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is permitted when it's safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted when it's safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is attached to slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: A car with bright headlights is driving toward you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Glance toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the oncoming car passes. This will protect your eyes from being blinded.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down to safely handle these curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means "stop."

questions.question: Your tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times.
Press the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the accelerator and do not brake. Let the car slow by itself. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How can you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the road is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.
When there is a red traffic light.

questions.explanation: You must stop completely at a red traffic light. You must also always obey a police officer who is directing traffic, even if signs or signals say something different.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to let you pass.
Drive very close to the parked cars to give more room to moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car without looking. A parked car's driver may start moving without seeing you.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Do not drive through it. Turn around and take another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through it. Turn around and take another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded water. Even shallow water can hide dangers. If you see a flooded area, turn around and find a different way to reach your destination.

questions.question: Motorcycles and scooters are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss or hide in your blind spot. Car drivers must always look for motorcycles and scooters.

questions.question: Which of these can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair driving. These include tranquilizers, sedatives, illegal drugs, and over-the-counter cough syrups, cold tablets, and allergy medicines that contain alcohol, codeine, or antihistamines.

questions.question: When you leave a parking spot to enter traffic, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of other traffic.
Wait for two cars to pass, then enter the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of other traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for enough space to match the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.

questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors, as they cannot show everything behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Drive at the same speed as the other vehicle.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing, do it quickly and safely to get back to your lane. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: A bad suspension can cause:
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to stay aware of traffic behind you.
